title: Kernel and line terms are invariant under the complex differential
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and C an integer-indexed chain complex of R-modules. Fix i, linear maps α:C_i→R and β:C_(i−1)→R, and z∈C_i, w∈C_(i−1). Assume βd_i=α, d_i(z)=w, αd_(i+1)=0 and d_(i−1)(w)=0. Define S_i=ker α, S_(i−1)=ker β and S_j=top elsewhere. Define U_i=R·z, U_(i−1)=R·w and U_j=bottom elsewhere. Every differential d_jk maps S_j into S_k and U_j into U_k. Normalizations α(z)=β(w)=1 are not needed for this invariance claim.

proof.text: Off the chain shape d_jk is zero. On the chain shape j=k+1, check the kernel target k=i using αd_(i+1)=0 and k=i−1 using βd_i=α; all other kernel targets are top. For line terms check the source j=i using d_i(z)=w and linearity, j=i−1 using d_(i−1)(w)=0, and all other sources using U_j=bottom.

lean.statement:
theorem split_submodules_stable
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
    (i : ℤ) (α : C.X i →ₗ[R] R) (β : C.X (i - 1) →ₗ[R] R)
    (z : C.X i) (w : C.X (i - 1))
    (hd : ∀ x, β ((C.d i (i - 1)).hom x) = α x)
    (hdz : (C.d i (i - 1)).hom z = w)
    (hin : ∀ x, α ((C.d (i + 1) i).hom x) = 0)
    (hout : (C.d (i - 1) (i - 2)).hom w = 0) :
    (∀ j k (x : C.X j), x ∈ splitKernelTerms C i α β j →
      (C.d j k).hom x ∈ splitKernelTerms C i α β k) ∧
    (∀ j k (x : C.X j), x ∈ splitLineTerms C i z w j →
      (C.d j k).hom x ∈ splitLineTerms C i z w k)
